beats.body:
New, tidy tables: `people`, `upi_accounts`, `company`, `rehearsal_attendance`, `event_schedule`, `insurance_claims`
(and `vehicles` now has a `company_id`). Each table holds one kind of thing — so we must **join** them.
`NATURAL JOIN` combines two tables on **every column with the same name**: `SELECT * FROM table1 NATURAL JOIN table2;`

beats.ask: Every UPI handle with its owner: `people.name` and `upi_accounts.upi_id`, using `NATURAL JOIN` (both tables have `person_id`).

hints.skeleton: SELECT people.name, upi_accounts.upi_id FROM people ____ upi_accounts;

beats.body:
`INNER JOIN … ON` joins on the condition **you** choose (any comparison operator works):
```sql
SELECT * FROM table1 INNER JOIN table2 ON table1.c1 = table2.c2;
```

beats.ask: Nysa says she was rehearsing. Show `people.name`, `rehearsal_attendance.check_in`, `rehearsal_attendance.check_out` for everyone who checked in at `'City Stadium'` (join on `person_id`).

hints.skeleton: SELECT people.name, rehearsal_attendance.check_in, rehearsal_attendance.check_out FROM people INNER JOIN rehearsal_attendance ON ____ = ____ WHERE rehearsal_attendance.venue = 'City Stadium';

beats.body: `LEFT JOIN` keeps **every** row of the left table; when there's no match, the right side is `NULL`. `WHERE right.c IS NULL` finds the rows with **no** match.
